purpose: Branded game-concept boot reel that replaces the plain engine loading screen. Played by Assets/Scripts/View/IntroVideoView.cs on the default boot route.

story.method: webtoon-harness pipeline (research -> beat sheet -> reference-consistent frame prompts -> validate), executed manually
story.harness_note: The native webtoon-harness agent team could not be launched here: it requires CLAUDE_CODE_EXPERIMENTAL_AGENT_TEAMS=1, which is unset in this environment. Only its method was reused, not its runtime.
story.source_of_truth: docs/nan2026/01-game-overview.md (title, Dusk Warden, lantern-oil tension, abyssal Cinder Court)
beats: 1. Ember spark ignites in pitch black
2. Spark becomes the ember lantern, held aloft
3. Dusk Warden silhouette rises with the lantern
4. Wide reveal of the abyssal court of obsidian pillars
5. Molten cinders surge through the court
6. Heroic brand hold — Warden raises the lantern in the colonnade (final hold, carries the title lockup)
story.dropped_beat: 6. Heroic brand hold — the ORIGINAL render (frame06.png, 1254x1254, god-tibo-imagen/codex-cli) was rejected on review because the central subject read as a piece of fruit instead of the lantern-bearing Warden. The beat was cut and the title lockup moved onto beat 5. RESTORED 2026-08-09 (see revisions): regenerated on Higgsfield nano_banana_flash with frame03+frame05 as image references.

frames.cli: gti --provider codex-cli --prompt "<beat prompt + shared STYLE suffix>" --output frames/frameNN.png
frames.outputs: _workspace/current/design/intro-video/frames/frame01..06.png (all six on disk; frame06 is the 2026-08-09 Higgsfield regeneration, not the rejected 2026-08-06 render)
provider_findings: The default private-codex backend returned HTTP 429 (image quota exhausted on this account) for every attempt, including an 8-attempt backoff run that produced zero frames.

The codex-cli provider succeeds, but rejects image input ("The codex-cli provider does not support image input"), so cross-frame consistency is carried by a shared STYLE suffix appended to every prompt instead of a reference image.
observed_sizes: frame06: 1264x848 (2026-08-09 Higgsfield regeneration; the rejected 2026-08-06 render was 1254x1254)

assembly.pipeline: scale-to-cover + centre-crop to 16:9 -> per-frame Ken-Burns (zoompan, alternating push-in / pull-out, 1.8 s each) -> 0.6 s fade cross-transitions -> burned-in title lockup -> fade in/out

title_lockup.font: Assets/Resources/Fonts/HudKorean.otf (same Korean subset the HUD ships)

observed_output.audio: none — deliberate. WebGL browsers block unmuted video autoplay, so IntroVideoView.cs:256 sets audioOutputMode=None and bgm-intro plays underneath from Unity instead.

assembly.pitfall: Feeding the stills as looped streams (-loop 1 -t 1.8) makes zoompan emit d frames per input frame; the first assembled reel was 87 s. Inputs must be single still frames so zoompan's d= alone sets segment length.

integration.wiring: Assets/Scripts/View/GameBootstrap.cs builds the IntroVideoView child; GameDirector.Attach takes it as an optional trailing argument and calls Play() on the default boot route only.
integration.overlay_contract: ScreenSpaceOverlay canvas at sorting order 520, above CutsceneView (500). The boot route runs underneath, so no game state is gated on playback.
integration.skip: Any key / tap, or the ?intro=off query parameter. QA deep links (?mode=arena|prologue|campaign) never show the reel.
integration.webgl: VideoPlayer on WebGL can only stream from a URL, so the clip lives in StreamingAssets rather than Resources. A 4 s prepare timeout and a 20 s watchdog guarantee the intro always finishes even when the browser cannot decode the clip.
integration.tests: Assets/Tests/EditMode/IntroVideoViewTests.cs — asserts the boot-never-blocks invariant (always finishes, reports completion exactly once per Play cycle, Hide is silent, replay re-arms) and the StreamingAssets path contract.

qa.title_render_check: signalstats YAVG over the title band rises 33.3 -> 79.6 and over the Korean subtitle band 29.1 -> 64.4 between t=3.0 s and t=7.2 s, confirming both lockup lines rasterised (Hangul glyphs present in HudKorean.otf). [6-frame cut]
qa.title_render_check_5frame: Re-measured after the frame06 cut: bright neutral pixels (r>200,g>195,b>180, saturation<40) inside the 1280x200 title band at y=225 count 7051 at t=5.5 s versus 1 at t=2.0 s, so the lockup still rasterises over the new final hold.

beat6_restoration.tool: Higgsfield CLI @higgsfield/cli 1.1.23 (npm -g), model nano_banana_flash (Nano Banana 2, image)
beat6_restoration.cli: higgsfield upload create frames/frame03.png; higgsfield upload create frames/frame05.png; higgsfield generate create nano_banana_flash --prompt "<brand-hold prompt>" --image <id03> --image <id05> --aspect-ratio 3:2 --resolution 1k
beat6_restoration.why_this_tool: The blocker on the original beat was cross-frame consistency: the codex-cli provider REJECTS image input (see frames.provider_findings), so style had to ride a text-only STYLE suffix and the subject drifted into still-life. nano_banana_flash accepts image references, so frame03 (Warden silhouette) + frame05 (court + ember palette) anchor both subject and palette.
beat6_restoration.observed_output: frames/frame06.png 1264x848 (1.491 aspect — matches frames 01-04 at 1.500 more closely than frame05 at 1.777), 1253874 bytes
beat6_restoration.review: PASS on the exact axis that failed before — full-body hooded Warden, both arms raising the ember lantern, visible cloak/legs/boots, obsidian colonnade, clean near-black top third.
beat6_restoration.title_lockup_move: Restoring beat 6 put the lantern flare under the old y=h*0.34 lockup band and the gold Korean sub-line sat on the flare. Measured the cropped 1280x720 luma of frame06 per candidate y: title band 35.5 -> 17.4 and sub band 56.8 -> 28.2 moving to y=h*0.18. assemble.sh now draws at h*0.18 and records the measurement method.

revisions: 2026-08-06 — cut beat 6 (rejected "apple-looking" brand-hold render): frames/frame06.png deleted, assemble.sh made frame-list driven (FRAMES array), reel re-assembled at 5 frames / 6.6 s / 1432004 bytes.
